intent: Declares and implements JSON::Value, Bedrock's in-memory JSON document node (scalar, array, or object), including its exception hierarchy and small helper types for building and iterating it.

objects.name: JSON::Error
objects.role: base exception for JSON errors; captures a stack trace via SException

objects.name: JSON::TypeError
objects.role: thrown when a Value is accessed/cast as the wrong ValueType

objects.name: JSON::NotFound
objects.role: thrown when a keyed or indexed member does not exist

objects.name: JSON::InvalidArgument
objects.role: thrown for malformed caller input, e.g. a non-numeric path key

objects.name: JSON::ValueType
objects.role: discriminates which kind of JSON node a Value currently holds

objects.name: JSON::Value
objects.role: tagged-union JSON node: scalar storage plus shared_ptr-backed object/array storage and all accessors/mutators

objects.name: JSON::KeyValue
objects.role: move-only key/value pair used to build a Value object from an initializer_list

objects.name: JSON::_ArrayValue<T>
objects.role: adapter giving a Value's array begin()/end() for range-based for loops

objects.name: JSON::_ObjectValue<T>
objects.role: adapter giving a Value's object begin()/end() for range-based for loops

objects.name: JSON::logStackTraceOnEnsureTypeFailure
objects.role: thread_local debug flag toggling stack-trace logging on ensureType() failure

objects.name: operator<<(ostream&, const Value&)
objects.role: serializes a Value to a stream

misfits.why: mutable global-ish thread_local debug/diagnostics toggle declared inline in the core value-type header; reads like a logging switch, not part of the JSON data model
a generic JSON value type's merge API names a specific downstream consumer (SQLite) in its parameter; the behavior it selects is really just RFC 7386 JSON Merge Patch semantics
constructor-timing instrumentation adds a chrono::time_point member to every Value instance, even scalars that never touch it, purely to detect occasional slow map/vector-based construction
grants SAXHandler direct access to Value's private storage for fast construction; the source comment itself calls this out as 'Coupling++'

name_fit.note: core type is JSON::Value, but the file also carries the exception hierarchy, KeyValue, and the array/object range adapters, none named after Value

location_fit.note: sits correctly alongside Parser, Writer, SAXHandler, and Utils in libstuff/JSON

naming_quality.note: public API is descriptive and consistent; private members lack the repo's `_` prefix convention, and intValue/uintValue are two easily-confused fields disambiguated only by usingUnsigned
